title: Cohomology of a Zariski module agrees with that of its underlying abelian sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X_{\rm Zar}$ its small Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site], and $\mathcal M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\mathcal M_{ab}$ for the underlying sheaf of abelian groups on $X_{\rm Zar}$. For every $q\geq0$ there is a canonical isomorphism $H^q(X,\mathcal M)\cong H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal M_{ab})$, where the left side is the right derived functor of global sections in $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-cohomology] and the right side is the right derived functor of global sections in abelian sheaves [def-sc-zariski-cohomology]. In degree zero this is the identity of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$, and the isomorphisms are natural in every morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), line 1862 and proof: the comparison for any ringed site and every object, specialized to the small Zariski site of a scheme; naturality follows from the uniqueness of universal delta-functors in the proof

proof.text: For every positive degree, take a natural functor isomorphism from [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology], now represented by zariskiModuleAbelianCohomologyNatural. This supplies all positive-degree components. The degree-zero component is chosen separately and does not use this comparison.

For degree zero, the global-sections functor is left exact, so Mathlib rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf identifies its zeroth right derived functor with itself. The abelian Ext-zero comparison of [def-sc-zariski-cohomology] is constructed explicitly: compose Ext.addEquiv₀, the sheafification adjunction, the free-abelian-group adjunction whiskered over the opens category, and Yoneda. The resulting additive equivalence sends an Ext class to precisely the section evaluation in the statement. Its naturality follows from Ext.mk₀_comp_mk₀ and functorial evaluation. Whisker the derived-zero isomorphism with forget₂ and the Ext-zero isomorphism with toSheaf; the two section functors are definitionally equal. Compose these natural isomorphisms to define e 0. In the normalization equation, apply_symm_apply cancels the Ext-zero equivalence and its inverse, and rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf_inv_hom_id_app cancels the canonical map Γ to R⁰Γ. Choose the positive-degree components by natural-number case distinction, yielding the asserted family and its degree-zero identity.
